title: Introduction to Lord Shiva in 10 Minutes
notes: Each shot has narration lines. '|' splits a line into on-screen caption beats, *word* marks the highlighted word.

shots.v: Deep indigo cosmos, drifting stars, slow nebula.
lines: Before the mountains rose, | before the rivers ran, | there was only a deep | and endless *silence.*

shots.v: A golden damaru drum appears and beats; rings of light ripple outward.
lines: And then… | a single *drumbeat.*
The universe woke up, | and began to *dance.*

shots.v: Silhouette of Shiva meditating against a huge glowing moon-disc.
lines: At the heart of that dance | sits one who is perfectly *still.*

shots.v: Shiva revealed in colour. Title card: Shiva — Introduction in 10 minutes.
lines: This is *Shiva* —| Mahadeva, the *great* god.
He is one of the most beloved gods in Hinduism, | worshipped by hundreds of millions of people, | for thousands of *years.*
In the next ten minutes, | let us get to *know* him.

shots.v: Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva side by side; each lights up in turn.
lines: In Hindu tradition, | three great gods | care for the *universe.*
Brahma *creates* it.
Vishnu *protects* it.
And Shiva *transforms* it.

shots.v: A tree sheds golden autumn leaves, then bursts into spring blossom.
lines: He is often called the destroyer. | But this is not a destruction | to *fear.*
Like autumn leaves that fall | so that spring may come, | Shiva ends what is old, | so that something new can *begin.*

shots.v: Warm close portrait of a smiling Shiva, petals drifting.
lines: His very name means | the *auspicious* one —| the kind, the *gentle.*
And to those who love him, | he is the source, and the home, | of *everything.*

shots.v: Full figure of Shiva with trident, sunburst behind.
lines: Look closely at Shiva, | for everything about him | tells a *story.*

shots.v: Camera rises to the matted locks and topknot.
lines: His long, matted hair | is the hair of a *yogi* —| one who has left every comfort behind | to search for the *truth.*

shots.v: The crescent moon in his hair glows; moon phases arc across the sky.
lines: In it rests a crescent *moon,* | growing and fading, night after night —| a sign that he is the master of *time.*

shots.v: A sparkling stream springs from the topknot.
lines: From his locks springs the river *Ganga,* | flowing from heaven down to *earth.*

shots.v: Extreme close-up of the forehead; the third eye opens in a flash of light.
lines: On his forehead is a third *eye* —| the eye of wisdom, | which sees what ordinary eyes *cannot.*
When it opens, | all that is false burns *away.*

shots.v: The cobra Vasuki sways gently around his neck.
lines: Around his neck coils a *serpent,* | Vasuki.
Fear itself, | worn calmly as an *ornament.*

shots.v: Hero shot of the trident; its three points light one by one.
lines: In his hand is the *trishula,* | a trident with three points —| said to stand for creation, protection, | and *dissolution.*

shots.v: The damaru swings and beats, sending out rings of sound.
lines: Tied to it is the *damaru,* | a small drum whose beat | is the rhythm of the *cosmos.*

shots.v: Ash drifts across a calm Shiva; tiger skin and beads are highlighted.
lines: His body is covered in *ash* —| a reminder that everything in this world | will one day *pass.*
He wears a tiger skin | and rudraksha beads, | owning nothing, and needing *nothing.*

shots.v: Mount Kailash at dawn, snow falling, prayer flags of light.
lines: Shiva's home is Mount *Kailash,* | a snowy peak | high in the *Himalayas.*

shots.v: Shiva seated in meditation on the summit, aura breathing slowly.
lines: There he sits in deep meditation —| the *Adiyogi,* the very first yogi, | and the teacher of yoga *itself.*

shots.v: Sati in a golden palace turns toward the hermit; then Shiva alone, grieving, in falling snow.
lines: But Shiva is not *alone.*
His first love was *Sati,* | a princess who chose the wandering hermit | over all the riches of her father's *palace.*
When she was lost to him, | Shiva's grief shook the three *worlds* —| and he withdrew into silence | for a very long *time.*

shots.v: Parvati meditates in the snow as seasons pass; Shiva opens his eyes.
lines: Then Sati was born again | as *Parvati,* | daughter of the mountain king.
For years she meditated in the snow, | until even the great hermit | opened his eyes, and *smiled.*

shots.v: Shiva and Parvati together beneath a shower of petals.
lines: She became his wife, | his equal, | and his *strength* —| for Parvati is Shakti, | the energy that moves the *world.*

shots.v: Ganesha with his sweet, then Kartikeya with his spear.
lines: Their sons are *Ganesha,* | the elephant-headed remover of obstacles,
and *Kartikeya,* | the brave young commander of the gods.

shots.v: Nandi the white bull waits by a temple doorway, bell swinging.
lines: And waiting faithfully at the door | is *Nandi,* the gentle bull —| Shiva's mount, | and his most devoted *friend.*

shots.v: Family portrait on Kailash: Shiva, Parvati, Ganesha, Kartikeya, Nandi.
lines: So Shiva is both a hermit | and a *husband,* | a wanderer and a *father.*
He shows that a spiritual life | and a loving family | can belong *together.*

shots.v: Gods and demons pull the serpent-rope around a mountain in a milky sea.
lines: Long ago, the gods and the demons | churned the great ocean of milk, | searching for the nectar of *immortality.*

shots.v: A dark violet cloud of poison boils up from the waves.
lines: But before the nectar | came a terrible *poison* —| Halahala, | dark enough to destroy every *world.*

shots.v: Frightened gods fold their hands before calm Shiva.
lines: Terrified, | everyone ran to *Shiva.*

shots.v: Shiva lifts the swirling poison in his palm and drinks.
lines: Without a moment's doubt, | he gathered the poison in his palm… | and *drank* it.

shots.v: Parvati's hand at his throat; the throat turns deep blue.
lines: Parvati pressed her hand | against his throat, | and there the poison *stayed* —| turning it a deep, dark *blue.*

shots.v: Serene Shiva with glowing blue throat; the sea calms, light returns.
lines: From that day he was called *Neelakantha,* | the blue-throated one —| who takes in the world's bitterness | so that others may *live.*

shots.v: King Bhagiratha prays on one leg beneath a starry sky.
lines: Another story tells of King *Bhagiratha,* | who prayed for the heavenly river Ganga | to come down and bless the *earth.*

shots.v: A colossal waterfall of light plunges from the heavens.
lines: But her fall was so mighty | that it would have shattered the *ground.*

shots.v: Shiva stands beneath the torrent and catches it in his hair.
lines: So Shiva stood beneath her, | and caught the whole river | in his *hair.*

shots.v: A gentle river winds through green plains past lamps and temples.
lines: Through his tangled locks | she slipped down in gentle streams,
and became the river | that millions still call *Mother* | today.

shots.v: Nataraja revealed inside a blazing ring of fire.
lines: Shiva is also *Nataraja* —| the Lord of the *Dance.*

shots.v: The ring spins, sparks fly, the cosmos pulses in time.
lines: Inside a ring of fire | he dances the *Tandava,* | and the whole universe | moves to his *rhythm.*

shots.v: Each hand highlighted in turn: drum, flame, blessing.
lines: One hand holds the drum of *creation.*
Another holds the flame of *ending.*
A third is raised to say: | do not be *afraid.*

shots.v: Close on the dancing foot above a small crouching figure.
lines: And beneath his foot | lies a small figure called *ignorance* —| for this dance sets the soul *free.*

shots.v: Galaxies wheel; a tiny Nataraja silhouette at the centre.
lines: Stars are born, and stars fade. | Seasons turn. | All of it, they say, | is Shiva's *dance.*

shots.v: A temple sanctum: the Linga, lamps, flowers, a slow drip of water.
lines: In most temples, | Shiva is not shown as a person at all, | but as the *Linga* —| a simple, rounded stone.

shots.v: The stone becomes an endless column of light through the sky.
lines: It stands for a pillar of light | with no beginning and no *end* —| the formless, the *infinite.*

shots.v: Twelve lights ignite across a stylised map of India.
lines: Twelve especially sacred shrines across India | are known as the *Jyotirlingas,* | the lingas of *light* —| from Kedarnath in the snows | to Rameswaram by the *sea.*

shots.v: Shiva and Parvati slide together into one figure: Ardhanarishvara.
lines: And sometimes Shiva appears as *Ardhanarishvara* —| half Shiva, half Parvati, | in a single *body.*
A beautiful way of saying | that stillness and energy | are never truly *apart.*

shots.v: Storm clouds and lightning; Shiva fierce, third eye glowing.
lines: Shiva has many names, | and many *moods.*
In the oldest hymns, the Vedas, | he is *Rudra,* | the roaring *storm.*
As *Mahakala,* | he is the lord of time itself, | before whom even death must *bow.*

shots.v: Sunny meadow; a child offers a flower to a delighted Shiva.
lines: As *Bholenath,* | he is the innocent lord —| so simple-hearted | that a little love is enough to *please* him.
He blesses gods, humans, | and even demons, | whenever they call on him with *devotion.*

shots.v: Forest glade; deer, birds and Nandi gather around him.
lines: And as *Pashupati,* | he is the guardian | of every living *creature.*

shots.v: A devotee pours water over the Linga; bilva leaves, a lamp.
lines: That is why his worship is so *simple.*
A little water. | A few bilva leaves. | A heart that is *sincere.*
Mondays are his special day, | and the ancient city of *Kashi,* | on the banks of the Ganga, | is loved as his very own *home.*

shots.v: Maha Shivaratri: temple spires at night, hundreds of lamps, a full sky.
lines: Once a year comes *Maha Shivaratri,* | the great night of Shiva,
when devotees stay awake until dawn —| fasting, singing, | and *praying.*

shots.v: The five syllables light up one by one around a glowing Om.
lines: And on their lips | is one mantra of five syllables: | *Om Namah Shivaya.*
I bow to Shiva. | I bow to the light *within.*

shots.v: Montage: dancer, protector, mountain, heart.
lines: So, who is Shiva?
He is the dancer, | and the *stillness.*
The destroyer, | and the *protector.*
The lord of the snowy mountain, | and the quiet place | inside every *heart.*

shots.v: Calm Shiva at sunrise; three soft symbols appear.
lines: He teaches that endings | are not to be *feared,*
that even poison | can be held with *grace,*
and that true strength | is *gentle.*

shots.v: A child sits quietly; Kailash glows in the distance, then within.
lines: So the next time you sit quietly, | and take one slow breath… | you may find that Kailash | was never far *away.*

shots.v: Shiva meditating in full glory; end title Har Har Mahadev.
lines: Om Namah *Shivaya.*
